pageCache.text:
Requesting Leave of Absence
Education law states that parents do not have a right to take their child out of school for a holiday during term time. Only in exceptional circumstances may a Head Teacher grant permission for leave; and it is the Head Teachers decision on whether the absence is exceptional and how many days to approve.
Any unauthorised absence of 10 sessions or more in the last 10 school weeks will be issued with a Penalty Notice. The current fine is £80 for each parent for each child
(eg two parents with 2 children, 4 seperate fines will be issued).
If each £80 fine is not paid with in 21 days the amount increases to £160.
If a second penalty notice issued to the same parent for the same child within a rolling 3-year period will be charged at a higher rate of £160
On the third period of absence within a rolling 3-year period as penalty notice will not be issued and the parent will be refered to the Hampshire Legal Team for legal action to be taken.
Also, if any payments are not made within the timescales provided, the local authority will consider commencing proceedings in the Magistrates’ Court

Admissions - Pre School
we are not currently accepting applications for the School Year 2026-27.
For general information please call the main school on 01425 472338 or email adminoffice@poulner-inf.hants.sch.uk
Hello and welcome to the Pre-School page.
Our pre-school is located in the grounds of Poulner Infant School and by being part of the school we are able to use the school facilities, such as the hall, field, library and are able to take part in school events and special days.
We moved into our purpose build pre school in November 2024 and are enjoying being in our wonderful new learning environment.
We cater for up to 26 children per session and can take children from 2 years to 5 years. We offer a morning session and an afternoon session with the option of staying for lunch if required. A cooked lunch is available to order daily at an additional charge.
We provide a stimulating and caring environment where each child is supported as an individual to learn and develop at their own pace.
We aim to ensure that each child:
Our pre-school 'Little Acorns' is overseen by the school Head Teacher Mrs Jo Conner.
Little Acrons is led by Lead Early Year Teacher, Mrs Jess Moses. Jess has extensive experience in Early Years and holds a Masters Degree in Education, specialising in learning through play in the Early Years. She is also a trained Therapeutic Play Practitioner.
Mrs Alex Peters is the Little Acorns Supervisor. She has a wealth of experience in Early Years practice; she trained as a Norland Nanny and has a degree focused on supporting children with Special Needs.
The staff team is made up of Level 2 and Level 3 practitioners. All staff contribute to and receive CPD alongside school staff and as a smaller team to keep up to date with new ideas, developments and training. The Little Acorns team have developed the room environment to create a
home-from-home rather than a classroom feel in line with the Curiosity Approach. We nurture our Little Acorns and aim to inspire a love of learning using developmentally appropriate methods.

Breakfast and After School Club
A limited number of spaces are available for pre school children aged 3 and over at our Breakfast and After School Clubs, please note that Early Years Funding cannot be used in payment of these sessions.
These sessions are offered following a discussion between the parent and pre school and agreement from the Head Teacher. For more information on these sessions please contact the school office.
For more information about early years funding please click on the following link https://www.childcarechoices.gov.uk/
If you would like further information please contact us on 01425 472338 or
email adminoffice@poulner-inf.hants.sch.uk

We look forward to meeting you soon.

Curriculum
Poulner Infant School Curriculum
We are proud to work as a team to provide a happy, safe, stimulating and creative environment in which to learn and grow. Central to our ethos is our commitment to value and nurture each child as an individual to enable them to achieve their best and develop an enthusiasm for lifelong learning.
We pride ourselves on ensuring we provide a broad and balanced curriculum that reflects our school’s vision and Values and is rich in experiences and opportunities for children to extend their skills of enquiry. We also try to use our local surroundings to support our learning. We follow the programmes of study in the National Curriculum 2014.
We try, where possible, to link up learning through overarching themes or topics. This helps to give learning a context and a purpose. We also recognise the importance of learning outside the classroom.
We deliver a programme of enrichment and experiences that all children receive as part of their Poulner Journey. Our extensive grounds include a huge field for sport and play, forest space and vegetable patch for outdoor learning. We have an attractive main playground with a gym trail and play equipment to enhance imaginative play. Teachers plan active “hands-on” learning opportunities that challenge thinking. Work is planned to meet the needs of every child and our aim is for pupils to become confident, motivated and enthusiastic learners for life. Visitors are welcomed into school and nursery to talk to our children about their expertise in an area of learning and educational trips are organised to further develop and reinforce their experience of a topic.
Inclusion is important to us, children with identified Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) access additional provision and support to help them achieve specific targets to help them progress. These targets are carefully monitored and parents and carers are updated as part of our commitment to working together to support learning.
